prerequisites: This course builds on Analysis I (B-KUL-H01A0B)
Participation certificate in a calibration test is required for courses in the Bachelor of Engineering Science program.

learning_outcomes.text: The student can set up simple mathematical models that lead to differential equations.

The student can solve first-order differential equations, as well as linear differential equations with constant coefficients, simple linear differential equations with non-constant coefficients, and simple non-linear differential equations.

The student can convert higher-order linear differential equations into a system of first-order differential equations. He/she understands and can apply the different methods for solving systems of linear differential equations with a constant matrix.

The student has acquired knowledge and insight into the following basic concepts of mathematical analysis: integral over a curve and a surface, line integral and surface integral, convergence of series and power series. He/she recognizes these concepts and can apply them to realistic problems.
The student has mastered the concepts from vector analysis. He/she masters the basic techniques in this discipline and can apply them.
The student can mathematically formulate, solve, and interpret the results of optimization problems with and without constraints.
The student can use mathematical software in all these domains to perform calculations and graphically represent the results.

syllabus_topics: exact differential equations and integrating factors
Chapter 3: Systems of linear differential equations
theory of systems of linear differential equations
Chapter 4: Integrals over curves and surfaces
length of a curve, natural parameterization
integrals of functions over a curve and over a surface
line and surface integrals, calculation of work and flux
theorems of Green, Stokes, and Gauss
solving differential equations with power series
problems without constraints, characterization of critical points
equality constraints, elimination method and Lagrange multiplier method
Session 1: introduction to the computer program to be used
Session 5: integrals over curves and surfaces, line integrals, surface integrals
Session 6: integrals over curves and surfaces, line and surface integrals, applications (computer-based)
assessment_rules: The permanent evaluation consists exclusively of exercises and accounts for 4 of 20 points. It is open book, with an electronic course text and computer programs available on PC. The exam consists of exercises and theory and accounts for 16 of 20 points; it is closed book, but a formularium is provided. A resit for the permanent evaluation component is possible upon student request; new points will be used, otherwise the first attempt's points are carried over. The exam resit is similar to the first attempt.
